Mahendra Singh Dhoni officially ended his playing career on November 17, 2026 , retiring from the Indian Premier League (IPL) on the retention deadline day for 2027 season.
Dhoni’s IPL career began with the inaugural edition in 2008. He represented Chennai Super Kings (CSK) for 17 seasons, leading the franchise to five IPL titles in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023. He also spent two seasons with Rising Pune Supergiant in 2016 and 2017, when CSK were suspended from the tournament.
Having already retired from Test cricket in December 2014 and limited-overs internationals in August 2020, he will now transition from an active player to the role of Team Mentor for the five-time IPL champion.
The 45-year-old leaves behind an enduring legacy as a leader, finisher and one of the most influential figures in the tournament since its inception.
CSK made him the costliest buy at the 2008 IPL auction at $1.5 million and named him captain from the opening season. Over two decades, he guided CSK to 10 IPL finals and 12 playoff appearances. He established them as the league's most consistent franchise.
Under his captaincy, CSK gained five IPL trophies, the joint-most by any captain alongside Rohit Sharma.
He also became the first skipper to successfully defend an IPL crown with back-to-back titles in 2010 and 2011, while adding two Champions League T20 titles in 2010 and 2014.
During CSK’s two-year suspension in 2016 and 2017, Dhoni represented Pune, captaining Rising Pune Supergiant in 2016 and playing under Steve Smith in 2017, when the side lost the final to Mumbai Indians by one run.
Across his storied IPL career, Dhoni has accumulated 5,439 runs in 278 matches at an average of 38.30 and a strike rate of 137.45. He also holds the record for the most dismissals by a wicketkeeper in the tournament’s history. For CSK specifically, he finished as the franchise’s most capped player with 272 appearances and second-highest run scorer with 5,314 runs.
Though he never scored an IPL century, he scored 24 half-centuries with a career-best score of 84 not out in 2019, a season where he averaged 83.20. His finest campaign with the bat came during CSK’s 2018 comeback, when he scored 455 runs at an average of 75.83 and a strike rate of 150.66. In 2023, he became the first player to feature in 250 IPL matches. Batting only at the death following a knee surgery in 2024, he hammered 161 runs off 73 balls at a strike rate of 220.54, the highest of any season in his career, with 14 fours and 13 sixes. He also went past 250 IPL sixes that season.
In the latter stages of his career, Dhoni had gone through several leadership changes and setbacks. Ahead of IPL 2022, he handed over the captaincy to Ravindra Jadeja, only to reclaim the role midway through the season following a poor start.
He stepped down again on the eve of IPL 2024 to pass the baton to Ruturaj Gaikwad, though an injury to Gaikwad in 2025 forced Dhoni back into the captain’s seat as CSK finished at the bottom of the table for the first time.
His continuous battle with recurring knee issues since 2023 had led to Dhoni missing the entire 2026 season due to calf and thumb injuries. It also marks the first IPL edition where he did not play a single match, before taking the lap of honour at Chepauk on May 18.
His reputation as a finisher was built on countless memorable performances, particularly his ability to remain calm in tense run chases and deliver under pressure. His trademark helicopter shot, powerful hitting in the final overs and remarkable awareness of match situations made him one of the most recognisable batters in the league.
Beyond his batting numbers, Dhoni’s wicketkeeping and cricketing intelligence also played a major role in CSK’s success. His sharp reading of the game, innovative field placements and ability to anticipate opposition strategies often gave his side an advantage in closely contested encounters.
The transition into a mentoring role comes at an important juncture for Chennai Super Kings, who are preparing for a renewed campaign following disappointing recent seasons. The franchise failed to qualify for the playoffs in the last three seasons and has consequently undertaken significant changes to its coaching and support staff ahead of IPL 2027.
Dhoni will be part of a revamped coaching setup headed by former India fast bowler Zaheer Khan as head coach. The support staff will also include assistant coaches Albie Morkel, Gareth Batty and Sridharan Sriram, bowling coach Mohit Sharma and fielding coach James Foster.
Beyond IPL, as captain of the Indian national team, he achieved a historic distinction by becoming the only captain to win all three major ICC white-ball trophies: the inaugural ICC T20 World Cup in 2007, the ICC Cricket World Cup in 2011 and the ICC Champions Trophy in 2013.
He represented India in 90 Tests, 350 One-Day Internationals and 98 T20 Internationals, accumulating more than 17,000 international runs while establishing himself as one of the finest wicketkeepers of his generation.
